title: Changes That Never Clash — Libraries That Agree in the End
description: Conflict-free replicated data types told at the loan desks of the scholars' coast: one scholar's deposit, a table of pebbles at every library with a column for each library, merged by taking the larger pile, and what counts, corrections and lists can and cannot be kept that way.
question: Can some changes be combined in any order, any number of times, and still come out the same everywhere, so that they never clash and no one ever needs to coordinate?
how: We find out by exploring how the libraries of the scholars' coast kept count of the scrolls one visiting scholar had out against a single deposit, without ever meeting to settle it.
credit: Shapiro, Preguiça, Baquero & Zawirski 2011 · the same authors' comprehensive study, 2011
